source.title: File:An Eurasian Marsh Harrier - Adult Male in flight (50572292483).jpg
source.author: Hari K Patibanda
source.description: Also known as the Western Marsh Harrier, these are large birds of prey that are predominantly found near wetlands or border marshlands. i.e. the areas around the river or lake banks where there are some kind of water birds. There are several pictures of this bird hunting egrets, herons, ducks and other small water birds - whether it was successful in the kill or not is unknown. The bird also hunts small birds, reptiles like lizards, frogs and small mammals like voles and rats. This is a winter visitor to the Subcontinent coming from Europe, and central Asia. Thanks in advance for your views and feedback. Much appreciated.

app.author: Hari K Patibanda

source.title: File:A male Pallid Harrier flying away from us early morning (50536689517).jpg
source.author: Hari K Patibanda
source.description: A few days ago, I had stumbled upon the communal roost of this species and found several. So we headed there early morning before sunrise to catch them in the good light with the sun against them. But only few of them remained with the rest flew away. The male was ready to fly and was very shy. It was perched on a eye height pole close to the road. We couldn't believe our luck and hoped for a full frame shot with a beautiful background. But if something is too good to be true, it is! The bird simply flew away east into the sun. Thanks in advance for your views and feedback. Much appreciated.
source.objectName: A male Pallid Harrier flying away from us early morning (50536689517)

source.title: File:Beautiful Montagu's Harrier in Flight (51042548717).jpg
source.author: Hari K Patibanda
source.description: As the light was fading during the sunset, we sighted maybe a dozen harriers landing one by one. A highlight was the presence of 2-3 sub-adult Montagu's harriers. The fully adult males like this one seem to have an issue with the sub-adults that they would chase them several times - short chases kind of meant to disturb the resting sub-adult. I am not sure why, but maybe its like sibling fight. This adult chased 2 sub-adults away and then made a full long circle (in this shot) to find a nice spot to roost. We sighted ~15 harriers in total which seemed comfortable with us as long as we sat in our vehicle. When we tried step out and crawl closer, they had little patience for our antics and flew away. Many thanks in advance for your views and feedback. Much appreciated.

source.title: File:A Montagu's Harrier Taking Flight (51621854680).jpg
source.author: Hari K Patibanda
source.description: Sighted a pair of Montagu's Harriers roosting in the fields during our morning trip. Both were females and we found them in the fog on a farm post. They took off as soon we got a tad closer. These are migrant Harriers from Central Asia and this year they are quite early. Normally, we sight them beginning Oct end and in good numbers towards end Nov onwards till Feb. These Harriers are grassland hunters and hunt small birds, reptiles and large grasshoppers. Thanks in advance for your views and feedback.
